Quantum entanglement is a physical phenomenon that occurs when a group of particles is generated, interact, or share spatial proximity in a way such that the quantum state of each particle of the group cannot be described independently of the state of the others, including when the particles are separated by a large distance. It is significant in the field of physics because it challenges classical notions of locality and realism, demonstrating that particles can remain connected so that actions performed on one can instantaneously affect the other, regardless of the distance separating them. This principle is foundational for emerging technologies such as quantum computing, quantum cryptography, and quantum teleportation.
